name: the-panel-holds-through-a-slip-off-either-edge
description:
The reporter parks the pointer on the panel's left border and the panel disappears and reappears, over and over. A grace cap closed it after 1.2 seconds of the pointer sitting in the tolerance band; the arming strip underneath then revealed it again, and the pair repeated. The panel's own window buttons live on that border, so the dots were unclickable for the same reason - the panel slid out from under the pointer on its way to them.

The lab has no cap. It looks once, 280ms after the pointer leaves, and a pointer inside the expanded rect keeps the sidebar open for as long as it stays (swipe-lab.html:5368-5375).

Both edges are read here. The docked one is the reporter's; the trailing one is the zone they asked for, where the pointer is off the sidebar and the sidebar stays.

assertions.label: neither-slip-closed-the-panel
assertions.desc: The panel prints this whenever it starts sliding out. A pointer resting in the band on either side must not produce one.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: sidebar overlay revealing at width
assertions.label: and-it-never-had-to-be-revealed-twice
assertions.desc: The PANEL's own line, not the edge zone's. The zone prints its intent before asking, and a re-entry with the panel already up is answered by cancelling the pending hide - so the zone's line appears twice on a run where nothing reopened. Only Show prints this one, so a second means the first closed and the strip brought it back.
